input.question: Why are there so many new medical breakthroughs in the news, but practically none of them ever become legitimate cures.
input.ground_truth: Because a breakthrough towards a cure is just one brick in the road, but it's what gets highly touted by the media because it's easy to point out. A team of scientists working in lab conditions come up with something promising and release their findings. Someone in the media sees this paper and turns "Disease has possible vulnerability!" and turns it into "CURE IS IMMINENT!!!1!" What they don't say is that it will take another few years of research, plus another few years of study, then another few years to create a human-safe cure (doesn't do anyone any good to cure the disease if it kills the patient as well), and then a few more years to figure out how to produce it at profitable levels.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: Why are there so many new medical breakthroughs in the news, but practically none of them ever become legitimate cures.

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you are building a big, tall tower with blocks. Every day, you try to put new blocks on top to make it even taller. Sometimes, you find a really cool new block that looks like it might help the tower stand better. But, sometimes that new block doesn’t fit quite right, or it falls down, or you realize you need a different shape.

In medicine, scientists are always trying new "blocks" — these are new ideas or medicines they think might help sick people. They tell everyone about their new block because they are excited and want to share what they are trying.

But, before a new medicine or treatment can really help everyone, scientists have to make sure the block *really* works and is safe. They have to test it many, many times with lots of people, like making sure the block fits perfectly and won’t make the whole tower fall over. This takes a long, long time and sometimes the block doesn’t work as well as they hoped.

So, we hear about lots of new ideas (blocks), but only a few of them actually become real, safe cures that help everyone. It’s because scientists have to be super careful to make sure the new medicine is truly good and safe before everyone can use it.
